source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

title: How do you feel when someone says 'no'?

lines.en: Hello and welcome to 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
lines.zh: 大家好，歡迎收聽 BBC 學習英語的《6 分鐘英語》。

lines.en: I'm Georgie.
lines.zh: 我是 Georgie。

lines.en: And I'm Neil.
lines.zh: 我是 Neil。

lines.en: Don't forget you can find vocabulary, definitions and a worksheet for free on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 別忘了，你可以在我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 免費找到單字、定義和練習單。

lines.en: So Neil, today we're talking about rejection.
lines.zh: Neil，今天我們要談的是「被拒絕」。

lines.en: So, rejection means saying no to someone or refusing to accept their idea or suggestion.
lines.zh: rejection 的意思是對某人說不，或拒絕接受他們的想法或建議。

lines.en: Neil, how do you feel about rejection?
lines.zh: Neil，你對被拒絕有什麼感覺？

lines.en: Well, nobody likes rejection.
lines.zh: 嗯，沒有人喜歡被拒絕。

lines.en: But I think as you get older, you get used to it.
lines.zh: 但我覺得隨著年紀增長，你就會習慣了。

lines.en: And probably it's quite a good thing to experience rejection, even if it doesn't feel nice.
lines.zh: 而且經歷被拒絕可能是件好事，即使感覺不太好。

lines.en: Yeah, I agree.
lines.zh: 對，我同意。

lines.en: We can't always get what we want, can we?
lines.zh: 我們不可能總是得到想要的，對吧？

lines.en: We can't, no.
lines.zh: 確實不行。

lines.en: In this podcast, we'll be learning about a new internet trend called rejection therapy and how people are using it to help them to be more confident.
lines.zh: 在這集節目中，我們會認識一個叫做「拒絕療法」的網路新潮流，以及人們如何用它讓自己更有自信。

lines.en: OK. Let's start with our quiz question, Georgie.
lines.zh: 好，Georgie，我們先從問答題開始。

lines.en: Lots of famous people have faced rejection in their lives before they became successful, but which of these things did not happen to the animator Walt Disney before he became successful?
lines.zh: 很多名人在成功之前都曾遭遇拒絕，但以下哪一件事「沒有」發生在動畫家華特・迪士尼成功之前？

lines.en: Was it: a) he lost his job as an artist, b) his first business ran out of money, or c) his first full length film was a failure?
lines.zh: 是 a) 他丟了畫家的工作、b) 他的第一個事業資金用光了，還是 c) 他的第一部長片失敗了？

lines.en: I've got no idea, but I'm going to go with a) he lost his job as an artist.
lines.zh: 我完全不知道，但我選 a) 他丟了畫家的工作。

lines.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
lines.zh: 好，節目最後會揭曉答案。

lines.en: OK Neil. So, most people don't like being rejected, but one thing to try might be something called rejection therapy.
lines.zh: 好的 Neil。大多數人都不喜歡被拒絕，但有一個可以試試的方法，叫做「拒絕療法」。

lines.en: It's a social media trend where people record themselves talking to strangers and sometimes being rejected.
lines.zh: 這是一個社群媒體潮流，人們拍下自己跟陌生人說話、有時被拒絕的過程。

lines.en: OK. That sounds quite interesting, but let's find out how it works in practice.
lines.zh: 好，聽起來蠻有趣的，我們來看看實際上是怎麼進行的。

lines.en: Hannah Gelbart, host of the BBC World Service podcast What in the World, had a go at the trend.
lines.zh: BBC 國際台 podcast《What in the World》的主持人 Hannah Gelbart 親自試了這個潮流。

lines.en: Let's see how she got on.
lines.zh: 來看看她的表現如何。

lines.en: Hey, can I come sit down at your table?
lines.zh: 嘿，我可以坐到你這桌嗎？

lines.en: Yeah.
lines.zh: 可以啊。

lines.en: Hey, how's it going?
lines.zh: 嘿，最近好嗎？

lines.en: Good, thank you.
lines.zh: 很好，謝謝。

lines.en: How's your day gone?
lines.zh: 你今天過得怎樣？

lines.en: Good afternoon. How are you doing?
lines.zh: 午安，你好嗎？

lines.en: Can I drive your cab?
lines.zh: 我可以開你的計程車嗎？

lines.en: Can I? Can I get behind the wheel?
lines.zh: 可以嗎？我可以坐駕駛座嗎？

lines.en: Don't be silly...!
lines.zh: 別傻了……！

lines.en: Coming somewhere else to try and face my fears...
lines.zh: 換個地方，試著面對我的恐懼……

lines.en: maybe do a bit of shopping.
lines.zh: 或許順便逛逛街。

lines.en: I was wondering, can I have a nap in one of these beds?
lines.zh: 我想問一下，我可以在這其中一張床上小睡一下嗎？

lines.en: Can I just try it out?
lines.zh: 我可以試躺一下嗎？

lines.en: Wow – I didn't expect that one to be a yes!
lines.zh: 哇，沒想到這個竟然答應了！

lines.en: Well, it seems like people were pretty nice to Hannah in those examples.
lines.zh: 嗯，從這些例子看來，大家對 Hannah 都還蠻友善的。

lines.en: Yes. And she talks with psychologist Claudia Hammond about how she felt during the experiment.
lines.zh: 對，她還和心理學家 Claudia Hammond 聊了她在這次實驗中的感受。

lines.en: And actually walking up to the first person, I felt my adrenaline really, really spiking.
lines.zh: 真的走向第一個人的時候，我感覺我的腎上腺素飆得超高。

lines.en: I'm not a socially anxious person.
lines.zh: 我不是個有社交焦慮的人。

lines.en: I think I'm really confident.
lines.zh: 我覺得自己蠻有自信的。

lines.en: But that first thing really scared me.
lines.zh: 但第一次真的把我嚇到了。

lines.en: And once I'd done one, the second one came easier and the third one came even easier. And you know, by the fourth time I didn't even mind it whether they said yes or no.
lines.zh: 做完一次之後，第二次就容易多了，第三次又更容易。到了第四次，我甚至不在乎對方答應還是拒絕。

lines.en: Hannah says that when she walked up to the first stranger in the video, she felt her adrenaline spiking.
lines.zh: Hannah 說，影片中她走向第一個陌生人時，感覺腎上腺素飆升。

lines.en: If something spikes, it increases sharply.
lines.zh: 如果某樣東西 spike，就是它急遽上升。

lines.en: Hannah is not generally a socially anxious person.
lines.zh: Hannah 平常並不是有社交焦慮的人。

lines.en: Someone who is socially anxious is nervous or worried about speaking to other people.
lines.zh: socially anxious（有社交焦慮的）的人，會對和別人說話感到緊張或擔心。

lines.en: Each time Hannah tried to speak to a new person, she says, it came easier.
lines.zh: Hannah 說，每次她試著和新的人說話，都變得更容易。

lines.en: Come easier is an informal way to say something is easier to achieve.
lines.zh: come easier 是口語說法，表示某件事比較容易做到。

lines.en: Now, this social media trend is called rejection therapy, but it's not a proper form of therapy.
lines.zh: 這個社群潮流雖然叫「拒絕療法」，但它並不是正式的治療方法。

lines.en: It hasn't been tested.
lines.zh: 它沒有經過驗證。

lines.en: And there are some criticisms of the videos because they involve filming your interactions with strangers, which people might not want.
lines.zh: 這些影片也受到一些批評，因為它們會拍下你和陌生人的互動，而對方可能並不願意。

lines.en: But people who post the videos say they boost their confidence.
lines.zh: 但發布影片的人說，這能提升他們的自信。

lines.en: So, why do people want to ask for rejection?
lines.zh: 那麼，為什麼人們會想主動去被拒絕呢？

lines.en: Psychologist Claudia Hammond has some ideas, which she shared with Hannah on the BBC World Service podcast What in the World.
lines.zh: 心理學家 Claudia Hammond 有一些看法，她在 BBC 國際台 podcast《What in the World》上和 Hannah 分享了。

lines.en: What we do know is that there is an increase in perfectionism.
lines.zh: 我們確實知道的是，完美主義正在增加。

lines.en: People are more worried now, younger people, about how other people are judging them.
lines.zh: 現在的人，特別是年輕人，更擔心別人怎麼評價他們。

lines.en: And so, I wonder whether that might make people more shy of speaking to strangers – worried that the people will, you know, not appraise them in a good way, and so doing something like this to try to counter that might feel
lines.zh: 所以我在想，這是否會讓人更不敢和陌生人說話——擔心對方不會給自己好的評價，因此做這樣的事來對抗這種心態，可能會讓人覺得

lines.en: like a positive step to people, that they're trying to do something.
lines.zh: 是積極的一步，覺得自己正在努力做些什麼。

lines.en: Also, they're fun to watch.
lines.zh: 而且這些影片看起來也很有趣。

lines.en: Claudia says there's an increase in perfectionism among young people.
lines.zh: Claudia 說年輕人的完美主義有增加的趨勢。

lines.en: Perfectionism is the feeling that everything you do needs to be perfect.
lines.zh: 完美主義就是覺得自己做的每件事都必須完美。

lines.en: Young people are also worried about how people will appraise them, which means judge them.
lines.zh: 年輕人也擔心別人會怎麼 appraise 他們，也就是怎麼評價他們。

lines.en: Deliberately looking for rejection might be an extreme way to become more confident, but it can lead to surprising discoveries.
lines.zh: 刻意去找拒絕可能是建立自信的極端方式，但它可能帶來意想不到的發現。

lines.en: Yes, and Hannah found that most strangers she spoke to were friendly and happy to help, so she didn't really experience rejection much at all.
lines.zh: 對，Hannah 發現她搭話的陌生人大多很友善、樂於幫忙，所以她幾乎沒怎麼被拒絕。

lines.en: OK. Georgie, I think it's time now for the answer to my quiz question.
lines.zh: 好，Georgie，現在該公布問答題的答案了。

lines.en: I asked you which rejection Walt Disney didn't experience before becoming successful?
lines.zh: 我問你，華特・迪士尼成功之前「沒有」經歷過哪一種拒絕？

lines.en: Yes, and I went for a) I don't think he lost his job as an artist.
lines.zh: 對，我選了 a)，我不認為他丟過畫家的工作。

lines.en: Well, actually, the answer was c) his first full length film, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, was not a failure.
lines.zh: 其實答案是 c)，他的第一部長片《白雪公主與七矮人》並沒有失敗。

lines.en: It was a huge success.
lines.zh: 它大獲成功。

lines.en: Wow! That was his first film?
lines.zh: 哇！那是他的第一部電影？

lines.en: That's really impressive.
lines.zh: 真的很厲害。

lines.en: It is.
lines.zh: 確實。

lines.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with 'rejection', which means saying no or refusing an idea or suggestion.
lines.zh: 好，我們來複習這集學到的單字，首先是 rejection，意思是說不，或拒絕一個想法或建議。

lines.en: The verb 'spike' means increase suddenly.
lines.zh: 動詞 spike 的意思是突然增加。

lines.en: Someone who is socially anxious is nervous or worried about speaking to other people.
lines.zh: socially anxious 的人會對和別人說話感到緊張或擔心。

lines.en: If something comes easier, it's easier to achieve.
lines.zh: 如果某件事 comes easier，就是它比較容易做到。

lines.en: 'Perfectionism' is the feeling that everything you do needs to be perfect.
lines.zh: perfectionism 就是覺得自己做的每件事都必須完美。

lines.en: And if you appraise someone, you judge them.
lines.zh: 如果你 appraise 某人，就是你在評價他。

lines.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but you can test what you've learned with the free worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 我們的六分鐘又到了，不過你可以到我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com，用免費練習單測驗你學到的東西。

lines.en: Thank you for joining us and goodbye.
lines.zh: 謝謝收聽，再見。

lines.en: Goodbye.
lines.zh: 再見。
